text:
sam: FYI team - noticed a p99 uptick on host path after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. looks correlated with high volume of tiny streams (avg len ~10). p99 jumped ~22% on decode-heavy requests.

sam: quick flame summary (alloc+syscall combined):
```
host-parse: +12%
grpc/small-write: +9% (writev stalls)
kernel-selection: picked fallback kernel for ~30% of small batches -> +18ms per request
kvcache: occasional eviction spikes but not dominant
```

ana: did the selector change the threshold logic? we pushed the nonuniform cost model last deploy.

sam: yes - moved from seq_len threshold to a learned score that tries to minimize GPU overhead. score is noisy for seq_len < 16 and tends to prefer a kernel with higher CPU path when batch_sz is tiny.

wei: that explains it. small batches + noisy score -> wrong kernel. two quick fixes: 1) add explicit fallback rule for avg_seq_len < 16 to force small-kernel; 2) smooth the score with an EWMA so single-sample noise doesn't flip selection.

taylor: + also we should emit selector telemetry: labels = [selected_kernel, batch_size, avg_seq_len, selector_score, is_kv_miss]. that'll let us query the flip rate and correlate to latency.

sam: agreed. I hacked a debug build to emit those metrics and replayed 10k synthetic tiny-stream calls. found selector flips on ~12% of batches where avg_seq_len=8..12.

ana: aside - networking also shows lots of `small-write` syscalls. could be our gRPC framing path doing multiple writes per frame. we tried write coalescing last year but maybe it's regressed.

wei: can you paste the small-write trace?

sam: snippet:
```
[grpc] call=abc123 writes: 4 syscall.writev calls (sizes: 64, 48, 32, 16)
[net] send latency: 1.8ms each -> stall compounding
[host-parse] waits for head frame -> delayed deserialization 12ms
```

wei: oof. combine coalescing at the framer with a quick fast-path that avoids allocating per-header and you'll get big wins. we should also track `small_write_count` per-request metric to join with selector flips.

taylor: another angle: kvcache evictions were noisy on that window. while not the main culprit, when eviction happened mid-batch decode we saw an extra memcpy and pinned CPU for ~20ms. suggest throttle reclaim or incremental reclaim to avoid synchronous spikes.

sam: filed PRs: 
- https://git.internal/r/runtime/selector-telemetry (adds metrics + EWMA smoothing)
- https://git.internal/r/runtime/framer-coalesce (coalesce small writes + header pooling)
- https://git.internal/r/kvcache/incremental-evict (soft-threshold + jitter)

deploy-bot: debug canary started for branches: selector-telemetry + framer-coalesce + incremental-evict. traffic split: 3% east-canary. build id=52021

ana: nice. one ask: when deploying, enable `selector.debug_sample=1%` to capture full context for a tiny fraction of requests so we can inspect per-request decision data without overwhelming metrics.

sam: enabled. after ~2h of 3% traffic I see: p99 improved from 270ms -> 235ms (still above baseline 210ms). selector flips dropped by ~9ppt in the tiny-stream cohort. small_write_count per-request dropped median from 3->1.

wei: good progress. remaining delta likely from kernel warmup + rare eviction bursts. we should also add kernel cold-start counter metric and a backoff to avoid switching kernels mid-stream.

taylor: agree. propose a short rule: once a request uses kernel X for first token, keep X for the request lifetime unless explicit failure. minimizes mid-request switches.

sam: implemented sticky-kernel patch locally, benched with tiny-stream replay: p99 now 220ms. deploy-bot: promoting canary to 20% for 6h observation.

deploy-bot: promoted canary -> 20% (job id=52021). monitoring hooks enabled: latency, selector_metrics, small_write_count, kvcache_evictions.

ana: if 20% holds for 6h with no regressions, let's merge and cut a follow-up note on the original selector change (it was squishy for small seqs). also add TASKs for longer-term work: better model for selector (TASK-1200), framer memory pooling (TASK-1201).

wei: I'll own TASK-1201. sam, can you validate the kernel sticky rule across seq_len spectrum (8..512) and ensure no perf cliff for medium seqs?

sam: yep will run synthetic suite and post results. closing for now, will update thread after 6h. :rocket:
